cover.caption: A Book for Everyone and No One

p1c1.caption: “Man is a rope, fastened between animal and Superman – a rope over an abyss.” — §57
p1c1.title: Zarathustra's Prologue
p1c1.rationale: The book's overture (150 paras, 4766 words): dawn sun-address (§1–10), forest saint + 'God is dead' (§11–28), marketplace Superman/Ultimate-Man sermons (§29–100), tightrope walker and buffoon (§106–107), corpse carried and buried in a hollow tree (§108–126, §137), companions-not-corpses resolve + rainbow (§127–142), eagle and serpent at noon (§143–150). Lead summary verified; beats the lead omitted (saint, Ultimate Man, hollow-tree burial) are staged in the scene's third beat and sky. The rope line is both the chapter's thesis and the inherited Direction-B motif.
p1c1.palette_role: Full Dawn arc (night→lapis→solar) — the ONLY P1 chapter allowed the whole spectrum: dawn gold for the address, storm-bone for the fall, star-night for the burial, noon gold for the animals. Bone text ≥10:1 on lapis.
p1c1.opener: Full-bleed scene (21:9, max-height 46vh, art above title, never behind text) → Cinzel part line 'Part the First · I' → Cinzel title (balanced, 2 lines) → pull-line in Spectral italic bone with gold § cite → sun-rule 14rem. No seal (scene replaces it per Rule 5). The only P1 opener with a horizon this wide — epic privilege, text-earned (150 paras, 5 movements).
p1c1.reading: Epic measure 40rem, gap 1.2em, calm throughout; no mid-text decoration per Rule 2. The 'I love him who…' anaphora (§59–74) and Ultimate-Man sequence (§88–100) carry their own rhythm; the closing cresting-sun mini-seal (App. A.0) lands after 'Thus began Zarathustra's down-going.'

p1c2.caption: “The child is innocence and forgetfulness, a new beginning, a sport, a self-propelling wheel, a first motion, a sacred Yes.” — §21
p1c2.title: Of the Three Metamorphoses
p1c2.rationale: The spirit's three stations — camel (reverent burden, desert), lion ('I will' vs the golden 'Thou shalt' dragon), child (innocence, play, self-propelling wheel). The chapter IS a triptych; the opener draws all three rather than choosing. Pull-line is the destination station, quoted whole.
p1c2.palette_role: Solar + serpent across the panels: camel in dimmed bone (burden), dragon-scale fragment in dense solar (the only P1 gold-field this saturated — greed of the old values), lion in solar/serpent, child in clear bone + solar wheel. Gold-field saturation is a one-chapter privilege.
p1c2.opener: Triptych emblem centered (3 panels, hairline dividers, solar/serpent/bone) → part line → title → pull-line (the child's Yes; longest pull-line in P1, earned as the chapter's destination) → sun-rule. Triptych reads left-to-right as metamorphosis; on 390px panels stack with preserved order.
p1c2.reading: Tablet measure 38rem; the 'What is heavy? / Or is it this…' litany (§3–10) reads as calm repeated verse — no special styling, gap 1.15em. Drop cap solar; mini-seal closes.

p1c3.caption: “Blessed are these drowsy men: for they shall soon drop off.” — §33
p1c3.title: Of the Chairs of Virtue
p1c3.rationale: Zarathustra visits the celebrated sleeper-sage: ten overcomings, ten reconciliations, forty thoughts, 'opium virtues', wisdom as dreamless sleep. The satire lands in §25–33 (laughter in the heart, contagious sleep, 'already they are lying down'). Pull-line is the verdict disguised as a blessing. Art must NOT wake the chapter up — hence the dimmed seal.
p1c3.palette_role: Dimmed bone + muted solar (lowest-saturation opener in P1; text still ≥10:1, dimming applies to seal/rule/drop-cap only, never body). Sleep made visible by restraint.
p1c3.opener: Seal 64px dimmed → part line → title → pull-line (the blessing-as-dismissal; driest wit in P1, set roman-italic as usual but allowed its full stop to land like a door) → sun-rule 12rem at 70%. Neighbor contrast vs p1c2 triptych (maximal art) and p1c4 (serpent-led, full-strength seal): this opener is deliberately the quietest so far.
p1c3.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.1em (slightly close-set: torpor). The wise man's numbered litany (§5–8, §19–20) flows as prose; no list styling (prose must not be restructured). Mini-seal closes.

p1c4.caption: “Purer and more honest of speech is the healthy body, perfect and square-built: and it speaks of the meaning of the earth.” — §32
p1c4.title: Of the Afterworldsmen
p1c4.rationale: Zarathustra confesses his own afterworldsman past (suffering God, coloured vapour, world as fiction), then the cure: overcome oneself, carry ashes to the mountains, kindle a brighter flame; the Ego learns honesty and titles the body. Pull-line is the chapter's cornerstone sentence — 'perfect and square-built' also describes the tablet opener itself.
p1c4.palette_role: Serpent-secondary lead (earth/body chapters): seal ring solar, drop cap serpent, pull-line bone. Ashes→flame carried by the Dawn-Ring's cresting sun, not by extra color.
p1c4.opener: Seal 64px full → part line → title → pull-line (the square-built body; architectural cadence, the chapter's cornerstone) → sun-rule 12rem. First serpent-led drop cap in P1 (earth chapters begin here) — neighbor contrast vs p1c3 (dimmed solar) and p1c5 (twin earth chapter, larger seal).
p1c4.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. The 'Believe me, my brothers!' passages (§13) need no styling — Spectral carries the address. Mini-seal closes.

p1c5.caption: “The body is a great intelligence, a multiplicity with one sense, a war and a peace, a herd and a herdsman.” — §4
p1c5.title: Of the Despisers of the Body
p1c5.rationale: The Self/Ego doctrine: soul is a word for something in the body; sense and spirit are the Self's instruments; the despisers serve a Self that wants to perish. Shortest metaphysical chapter in P1 (21 paras) — hence the large seal: small chapter, load-bearing idea. Pull-line is the doctrine in one sentence.
p1c5.palette_role: Serpent-secondary, deeper than p1c4 (seal 72px, drop cap serpent, pull-line bone). The herd/herdsman pair in the pull-line echoes the Prologue's herdsmen — palette stays earthbound, no solar field.
p1c5.opener: Seal 72px large → part line → title → pull-line (the great-intelligence sentence; four balanced pairs, set to breathe) → sun-rule 13rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c4 (same earth family, smaller seal) and p1c6 (transformation warmth): scale + pull-line cadence differentiate, not color.
p1c5.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.2em (aphoristic air for short paras). The Self-says/commands sequence (§9–13) flows as calm decree. Mini-seal closes.

p1c6.caption: “Once you had fierce dogs in your cellar: but they changed at last into birds and sweet singers.” — §13
p1c6.title: Of Joys and Passions
p1c6.rationale: Virtues must be one's own (unutterable, stammered), grown from passions: devils→angels, poison→balsam, dogs→birds — but jealous virtues turn scorpion-stings on the self, and one perishes by one's virtues. Pull-line is the chapter's miracle image. (Young-man echo: the fierce dogs return in p1c9 §20 — same cellar.)
p1c6.palette_role: Solar warmth returns (transformation chapter): solar drop cap, bone pull-line, seal full. The scorpion's jealousy (§21) is carried by prose, not color — no ember here (violence stays verbal until p1c7–p1c8).
p1c6.opener: Seal 64px → part line → title → pull-line (dogs→birds; the transformation image, alchemical and auditory at once) → sun-rule 12rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c5 (large seal, decree voice) and p1c7 (palest opener): standard seal + warm solar cap + the only cellar-to-sky pull-line in P1.
p1c6.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. The stammer passage (§5–6) and jealousy sequence (§18–22) read as-is; restraint lets the scorpion land. Mini-seal closes.

p1c7.caption: “A knot of savage serpents that are seldom at peace among themselves – thus they go forth alone to seek prey in the world.” — §19
p1c7.title: Of the Pale Criminal
p1c7.rationale: Parable before judges (form verified in full text, not inference): the pale criminal judged himself — his supreme moment; killing must be mercy justifying life; thought/deed/image of the deed; madness before (soul thirsting for the knife) and after (the image endured); guilt as lead; man as knot of serpents. Pull-line is the chapter's anatomy — and a dark mirror of the book's serpent device, kept verbal for that reason.
p1c7.palette_role: Bone-lead: desaturated bone-grey via color-mix (NOT a new hue) for seal-dim + drop cap; solar withheld to 60% in ring only. The scarlet judge stays verbal — no red drawn (Part I discipline; ember belongs to Part IV).
p1c7.opener: Seal 64px withheld → part line → title → pull-line (the knot of serpents; darkest image in P1, set in bone without gold emphasis) → sun-rule 12rem at 60%. Neighbor contrast vs p1c6 (warm solar) and p1c8 (blood-ink fire): this is the cold hinge between them — palest opener, deliberate.
p1c7.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. The judge-address passages (§5–7, §11) read as spoken parable; no courtroom styling (no tint bands, no speaker labels). Mini-seal closes.

p1c8.caption: “I should believe only in a God who understood how to dance.” — §21
p1c8.title: Of Reading and Writing
p1c8.rationale: Write with blood; aphorisms as peaks for the long-legged; courage making hobgoblins; looking down from exaltation; wisdom loving only warriors; love's madness and method; the dancing God; the Spirit of Gravity killed by laughter; learning to walk/run/fly. Pull-line is the chapter's creed and Part I's most quotable sentence. Blood-ink cap is the §81-spec exception.
p1c8.palette_role: Solar restored + ONE ember note (drop cap only, text-verified blood). The peaks (§7) stay verbal — no mountain drawn (rejected-theme territory; Part I is liturgy now, not mountaineering).
p1c8.opener: Seal 64px full → part line → title → pull-line (the dancing God; shortest pull-line in P1, maximum memorability) → sun-rule 12rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c7 (palest) and p1c9 (tree emblem): fire between frost and wood — ember cap + dancing pull-line + restored seal.
p1c8.reading: Aphorism air: measure 38rem, gap 1.3em (widest paragraph rhythm in P1 — peaks need valleys). Short paras breathe; no styling per para (no mod-N anything). Mini-seal closes.

p1c9.caption: “The more it wants to rise into the heights and the light, the more determinedly do its roots strive earthwards, downwards, into the darkness, into the depths – into evil.” — §4
p1c9.title: Of the Tree on the Mountainside
p1c9.rationale: The avoiding young man found leaning on a lone mountainside tree: invisible winds, roots striving into evil, distrust after ascent, contempt and desire climbing together, the tree waiting for lightning — the youth confesses envy of Zarathustra and is drawn along; then counsel (prisoners imagining freedom, noble vs good, keep holy the highest hope). Pull-line is the chapter's natural law; emblem draws its two directions.
p1c9.palette_role: Serpent + solar split (roots vs crown): root-wedge in night/serpent dark, crown in bone, waiting lightning in solar. The emblem stages the pull-line's law visibly: light above, evil below.
p1c9.opener: Tree emblem ≤120px → part line → title → pull-line (roots-into-evil; the chapter's law, quoted whole) → sun-rule. Neighbor contrast vs p1c8 (aphorism air, seal) and p1c10 (necrotic tablet): the only botanical emblem in P1; vertical tree against horizontal rules.
p1c9.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. Dialogue passages (§1–15) flow as narrative prose; the counsel (§17–29) likewise — no speaker styling. Mini-seal closes.

p1c10.caption: “There are preachers of death: and the earth is full of those to whom departure from life must be preached.” — §1
p1c10.title: Of the Preachers of Death
p1c10.rationale: Catalogue of death-preachers: the lustful/mortified, soul-consumptives, sweet-snatchers on straws, suffering-peddlers, anti-birth whisperers, pity-thieves, and the unrestrained-labour weary. Pull-line is the tolling opening sentence — the chapter's title restated as fact. Dimming distinguishes rot (p1c10) from pallor (p1c7, guilt) and torpor (p1c3, sleep): three different dims, three documented causes.
p1c10.palette_role: Dimmed bone necrotic (rot, not sleep): seal/rule/cap at 70%, body full bone. Yellow/black men stay verbal — no yellow or black fields drawn (would need new hues; the dimming IS the rot).
p1c10.opener: Seal 64px dimmed → part line → title → pull-line (the opening sentence itself — a tolling bell; only P1 pull-line taken from §1 verbatim whole) → sun-rule 12rem at 70%. Neighbor contrast vs p1c9 (vertical emblem) and p1c11 (martial brightness): horizontal dim tablet between image and blaze.
p1c10.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.1em (close-set catalogue air). The 'There are…' litany (§4–6, §9–13) reads as tolling prose. Mini-seal closes.

p1c11.caption: “You should love peace as a means to new wars. And the short peace more than the long.” — §7
p1c11.title: Of War and Warriors
p1c11.rationale: To the brothers in war: don't spare enemies, seek them; love short peace; let work be battle and peace victory; silence needs arrow and bow; the good war hallows causes; bravery over pity; sublime ugliness; pride in enemies; obedience that commands; man overcome. Pull-line is the chapter's most portable paradox. Blaze placement is deliberate: war-dawn between rot (p1c10) and the cold state (p1c12).
p1c11.palette_role: Solar martial (brightest tablet since p1c8): full seal, solar cap, bone pull-line. No steel drawn (no new hue for blades); the bowstring is the sun-rule itself, read taut.
p1c11.opener: Seal 64px full → part line → title → pull-line (short peace; the chapter's paradox engine) → sun-rule 12rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c10 (dim catalogue) and p1c12 (cold-idol emblem): bright martial tablet between rot and ice — the only 'war' voice in P1.
p1c11.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. Hortatory 'You should…' rhythm (§5–9, §17–19) needs no styling — imperatives carry. Mini-seal closes.

p1c12.caption: “The state is the coldest of all cold monsters. Coldly it lies, too; and this lie creeps from its mouth: ‘I, the state, am the people.’” — §3
p1c12.title: Of the New Idol
p1c12.rationale: The state as cold monster: creators made peoples, destroyers made states; stolen teeth and belly; confusion of tongues; the superfluous devoured and re-chewed; heroes lured; slow suicide called life; culture-theft and newspaper-bile; throne-madness; idol-stink — then the exit: break the window, free earth for great souls, and where the state ceases, rainbow and bridges to the Superman. Emblem draws both poles (idol + rainbow); pull-line is the lie itself.
p1c12.palette_role: Cold bone-grey idol (desaturated via color-mix) vs solar/serpent/ember rainbow hairlines — the ONLY rainbow in P1, text-verified §34. Idol cold, exit warm: the emblem stages the chapter's whole argument (cold lie → open air).
p1c12.opener: Smashed-idol emblem ≤120px → part line → title → pull-line (the cold monster's lie, quoted with its own voice inside) → sun-rule. Neighbor contrast vs p1c11 (bright martial seal) and p1c13 (marketplace tablet): the coldest image in P1 with the warmest exit (rainbow) — ice between blaze and buzz.
p1c12.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. The 'Just look…' anaphora (§20–22) and 'Avoid…' commands (§27–29) read as prophetic catalogue; the closing rainbow (§34) lands on calm prose + mini-seal.

p1c13.caption: “The experience of all deep wells is slow: they must wait long until they know what has fallen into their depths.” — §14
p1c13.title: Of the Flies of the Market-place
p1c13.rationale: Flight from the market-place: uproar of great men, stings of small ones; actors vs inventors; overthrow-as-proof; solemn buffoons demanding Yes/No; deep wells slow; solitude and the raw breeze; the fly-swat fate refused; poisonous praise; small souls' vengeance. Pull-line answers the title's buzz with the chapter's quietest sentence (the well also anticipates the hermit-well of p1c20 §12).
p1c13.palette_role: Solar standard (marketplace noon): full seal, solar cap. Flies stay verbal — no speck texture drawn (would read as noise/grain, fighting the calm-body rule). The well-depth is the pull-line's, not a color.
p1c13.opener: Seal 64px → part line → title → pull-line (the deep well; stillness quoted against a buzzing title — deliberate counterpoint) → sun-rule 12rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c12 (cold emblem) and p1c14 (forest intimate): standard bright tablet; the pull-line's slowness IS the variation (only stillness pull-line in P1's middle third).
p1c13.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.1em (breathless catalogue for the fly-passages §18–29, then the closing flight §35 exhales). No fly-speck styling — prose carries the swarm. Mini-seal closes.

p1c14.caption: “Do I exhort you to kill your senses? I exhort you to an innocence of the senses.” — §5
p1c14.title: Of Chastity
p1c14.rationale: Forest vs lustful towns; filth with spirit; animal innocence; chastity as virtue for some, near-vice for many; the bitch Sensuality in abstinence's heights and cold depths; tragedy-lust mistrusted; devils entering swine; shallow vs dirty truth; the heart-chaste who laugh at chastity itself. Pull-line states the doctrine as a corrected question. Intimate scale (18 paras) earns the small seal.
p1c14.palette_role: Serpent-led intimate (forest shade): serpent drop cap, small seal, bone pull-line. Sensuality's bitch stays verbal — no animal drawn (metaphor, not subject, per P1-C rejection).
p1c14.opener: Seal 56px small → part line → title → pull-line (the innocence distinction; question-and-answer in one breath) → sun-rule 11rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c13 (bright standard tablet) and p1c15 (no-drop hermit tablet): smallest seal in P1's middle third + serpent cap + forest voice — shade between buzz and hermitage.
p1c14.reading: Intimate measure 36rem, gap 1.15em. Parable-question rhythm (§11–12, §15–17) reads close and cool. Mini-seal closes.

p1c15.caption: “In your friend you should possess your best enemy.” — §10
p1c15.title: Of the Friend
p1c15.rationale: The hermit's arithmetic (one too many); I-and-Me needing the friend as third and cork; faith-in-others betraying self-faith; love leaping over envy; 'at least be my enemy'; war for the friend; honouring the enemy in him; nakedness feared; the arrow-longing; the sleeping friend's face as rough mirror; conjecturing pity; slave/tyrant unfit for friendship; comradeship→friendship. Pull-line fuses the war voice (p1c11) into love. No-drop opening is text-caused and recorded.
p1c15.palette_role: Bone standard (hermit clarity): full seal, bone pull-line, no cap color (no cap). The arrow (§13) and mirror (§14) stay verbal — drawn nowhere (metaphors, per discipline).
p1c15.opener: Seal 64px → part line → title → pull-line (best enemy; the chapter's paradox, war-voice in a love chapter) → sun-rule 12rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c14 (small seal, serpent cap) and p1c16 (large seal, ethnographic): standard seal + NO drop cap (only the second no-drop opening in P1) — the missing cap IS the variation, text-caused (quote-led).
p1c15.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. Opening without cap, then calm prose; the mirror passage (§14–15) needs no styling — the image holds. Mini-seal closes.

p1c16.caption: “A table of values hangs over every people.” — §5
p1c16.title: Of the Thousand and One Goals
p1c16.rationale: Many lands, many goods-and-evils: no people without evaluating, none evaluating as its neighbour; tables as overcomings and will to power; hard→praiseworthy→holy; Greek/Persian/germanic/loyalty tables; man the evaluator; evaluation as creation; creators must destroy; herd vs Ego; loving men naming good and evil; the praising/blaming monster with a thousand necks awaiting fetters and the one missing goal. Pull-line hangs the image over the whole chapter; large seal marks the hinge.
p1c16.palette_role: Solar monumental (survey chapter): large seal, solar cap, bone pull-line. The thousand-necked beast stays verbal — no monster drawn (a beast here would pre-empt Part IV's bestiary and p1c12's idol).
p1c16.opener: Seal 72px large → part line → title → pull-line (the hanging table; the chapter's image-axiom, foreshadowing p3c12's shattered tablets) → sun-rule 13rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c15 (no-drop standard) and p1c17 (admonitory standard): large seal + traveled opening + the only ethnographic voice in P1.
p1c16.reading:
Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. The quoted tables (§9–11) flow as prose (no blockquote styling in data — all

); the beast passage (§23–25) closes toward the mini-seal.

p1c17.caption: “May the friend be to you a festival of the earth and a foretaste of the Superman.” — §13
p1c17.title: Of Love of One's Neighbour
p1c17.rationale: Against neighbour-love as bad self-love: the consecrated You vs unconsecrated I; flight to the most distant; the fairer phantom; sponges for overflowing hearts; witnesses seduced into praise; lying about the unknown; solitude-as-prison; festivals of actors; the friend as festival and vessel; future-as-principle. Pull-line is the chapter's gift after its rebuke — and 'foretaste' disciplines the palette (no festal color).
p1c17.palette_role: Solar admonitory (standard brightness): full seal, solar cap. The festival stays verbal — no festal styling (festival grammar belongs to p4c18; a foretaste must not dress as the feast).
p1c17.opener: Seal 64px → part line → title → pull-line (festival of the earth; the warmest sentence in P1's middle third) → sun-rule 12rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c16 (large survey seal) and p1c18 (large threshold seal): standard seal between two larges — the calm step between survey and solitude.
p1c17.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. Rebuke-then-gift rhythm (§1–12 vs §13–17) reads on calm prose; the closing exhortation (§17) lands into the mini-seal.

p1c18.caption: “You must be ready to burn yourself in your own flame: how could you become new, if you had not first become ashes?” — §25
p1c18.title: Of the Way of the Creator
p1c18.rationale: Threshold sermon of creator-solitude (form verified in full text): going apart, the herd's inner voice, affliction-as-way, new strength/new right, self-propelling wheel, free-for-what, hanging one's will as law, the star in empty space, weary solitude, contempt's anguish, flying hated, shining despite dirt, guarding against the good/holy-simplicity/love's assaults, the paw with claws, self as worst enemy, seven devils, heretic/witch/prophet/villain, burning to become new, creating a god from devils, lover's contempt, perishing beyond oneself. Pull-line is the ordeal. (Self-propelling wheel echoes p1c2 §21 — same image, hotter context.)
p1c18.palette_role: Solar threshold (deepened, not embered): large seal, solar-deep cap via color-mix, bone pull-line. The flame is dawn-fire (Part I), not dusk-ember (Part IV) — the mix ratio is documented so the engineer holds the line.
p1c18.opener: Seal 72px large → part line → title → pull-line (burn in your own flame; the chapter's ordeal-stake, quoted whole with its question) → sun-rule 13rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c17 (standard calm) and p1c19 (twilight dialogue, small seal, no cap): large threshold seal + deepened cap + flame pull-line before the book's quietest dialogue.
p1c18.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.2em (threshold air: questions need silence around them). The question-litany (§6–12) reads as trial; the closing tears (§30) into the mini-seal.

p1c19.caption: “Are you visiting women? Do not forget your whip!” — §29
p1c19.title: Of Old and Young Women
p1c19.rationale: Twilight dialogue (form corrected per lead: NOT dance-voice): Zarathustra slinks through twilight hiding a little truth; an old woman at sunset asks for woman-spoken-to-women; his speech (riddle/pregnancy, means/child, danger/play, warrior's recreation, bitter sweetness, the child in man, plaything-precious-stone, bearing the Superman, bravery/honour in love, fear in love and hate, iron-to-magnet, I-will/He-will, perfected world, surface/torrent); her thanks-gift: the whip. Pull-line is the crack the whole chapter walks toward.
p1c19.palette_role: Twilight bone (latest hour before p1c22's dusk): seal 56px at 85%, rule at 85%, no cap, bone pull-line. Content note: the chapter's gendered satire is Nietzsche's text, quoted verbatim with citation; design takes no editorial position beyond the twilight staging the prose itself gives (shy twilight walk, sunset hour, confessional frame).
p1c19.opener: Seal 56px twilight-dimmed → part line → title → pull-line (the whip; the chapter's crack — quoted as the old woman's speech, cited) → sun-rule 11rem at 85%. Neighbor contrast vs p1c18 (large threshold blaze) and p1c20 (adder emblem): smallest, dimmest seal in P1's final third + no cap + dialogue voice — dusk between fire and fangs. DANCE-VOICE EXPLICITLY REJECTED per lead correction: this is twilight-dialogue/confessional, staged as frame-tale (walk → encounter → speech → thanks-gift), not dance.
p1c19.reading: Confessional measure 36rem (narrow — twilight closeness), gap 1.2em. Frame-tale rhythm (walk §1–7, speech §8–25, thanks §26–29) reads on calm prose; no speaker styling. Mini-seal closes.

p1c20.caption: “When did a dragon ever die from the poison of a snake?” — §1
p1c20.title: Of the Adder's Bite
p1c20.rationale: Parable + moral: adder bites the sleeping Zarathustra, recognizes his eyes, would flee; thanked for waking at the right time; deathly poison refused ('take your poison back — not rich enough'); disciples ask the moral: don't shame enemies with good-for-evil, prove their good; anger over shaming; curse back a little; shared injustice as half justice; little revenge human; declaring oneself wrong when rich; cold justice refused; justice as seeing love; giving everyone what is mine; the hermit-well no stone returns from. Emblem draws the bite-scene; pull-line is the rank-riddle.
p1c20.palette_role: Serpent-led parable (second serpent emblem after the triptych's lion panel; first pure-creature emblem): serpent body, bone leaves, solar eye + heat-dot, ONE ember tongue-flick (text-verified bite; minimal). Fig shade = night-wash behind leaves, flat, no gradient.
p1c20.opener: Adder emblem ≤120px → part line → title → pull-line (dragon vs snake; the chapter's riddle of rank) → sun-rule. Neighbor contrast vs p1c19 (dim twilight seal, no cap) and p1c21 (bright nuptial seal, solar cap): noon-heat emblem + serpent cap between dusk and wedding — fangs between cloak and torch.
p1c20.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. Long §1 (the whole bite-story in one para) then short morals (§3–13) — the shape IS the treatment (story, then verdicts). Mini-seal closes.

p1c21.caption: “It is a torch which should light your way to higher paths.” — §21
p1c21.title: Of Marriage and Children
p1c21.rationale: Marriage interrogated: the plummet-question (depth of soul); victor/self-conqueror fitness; animal/necessity/isolation/disharmony unfitness; victory longing for a child; building beyond, square-built; upward propagation; the garden; creating the creator; marriage as will-of-two for the more-than-two; superfluous marriage as filth/ease; heaven of the superfluous refused; saint-goose convulsions; dressed-up lies and wrapped wives; brief follies/long stupidity; best love as torch; bitter cup → Superman-thirst. Pull-line is the upward answer. (Self-propelling wheel §8 echoes p1c2/p1c18 — third toll of the image.)
p1c21.palette_role: Solar nuptial (standard brightness, torch-warmed): full seal, solar cap, bone pull-line. Plummet-depth and torch-height are both solar — one metal, two directions (no split palette: the chapter unites them).
p1c21.opener: Seal 64px → part line → title → pull-line (the torch; upward answer to the plummet's downward question) → sun-rule 12rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c20 (creature emblem, serpent cap) and p1c22 (dusk tablet, deepest gold): bright interrogative tablet between fangs and sunset — torch between shade and glow.
p1c21.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.15em. Question-then-catalogue rhythm (§1–9 asking, §10–20 exhibiting, §21–23 hallowing) reads on calm prose. Mini-seal closes.

p1c22.caption: “In your death, your spirit and your virtue should still glow like a sunset glow around the earth: otherwise yours is a bad death.” — §32
p1c22.title: Of Voluntary Death
p1c22.rationale: Voluntary death: dying at the right time (goal + heir); the hollow nut; death not yet a festival; consummating death with vows; battle-death second; grinning thief-death refused; no withered wreaths; rope-makers backwards; glory leaving honour in time; sour apples; poison-worm hearts; storm shaking the tree; preachers of speedy death; Jesus too early (desert, laughter, recanting unlived); child-in-man on life and death; free in death; sunset-glow death; becoming earth again; the golden ball thrown to friends. Pull-line states the test. Dusk-gold is the day's farewell before the finale's noon.
p1c22.palette_role: Dusk-gold derivation (solar 85/ember 15 via color-mix — text-verified sunset, §32; documented exception to P1's ember discipline, minimal and chapter-bound). Body stays bone-on-lapis; derivation touches seal/rule/cap only.
p1c22.opener: Seal 64px dusk-gold → part line → title → pull-line (sunset glow; the longest pull-line after p1c2/p1c9 — evening needs room) → sun-rule 12rem dusk-gold. Neighbor contrast vs p1c21 (pure-solar torch tablet) and p1c23 (finale white-gold blaze): the dusk hinge — deepest gold in P1, exhaling into the finale's noon.
p1c22.reading: Measure 38rem, gap 1.2em (evening air). The death-catalogue (§13–20) then the Jesus passage (§23–29, handled as prose, no styling) then the ball-throw close (§34–35) into the mini-seal.

p1c23.caption: “‘All gods are dead: now we want the Superman to live’ – let this be our last will one day at the great noontide!” — §51
p1c23.title: Of the Bestowing Virtue
p1c23.rationale: Part finale (52 paras): farewell to the Pied Cow, cross-road solitude, the staff with serpent coiled about a sun; gold's value (uncommon, useless, shining, bestowing); giver's glance; bestowing virtue; thirst to heap soul-riches; the fountain; healthy vs sick selfishness; degeneration suspected where bestowing lacks; upward way; body through history, spirit as herald; image-names; virtue's origins (river-heart, exalted will, hard bed, single will); new virtue as power with golden sun + knowledge-serpent; loyalty to earth; flown-away virtue led back; chance fought; body purified by knowledge; thousand untrodden paths; solitaries→people→Superman; the staff balanced; going-alone commanded; hating friends; plucking laurels; the falling statue; losing/finding; denial-then-return; the great noontide (middle course, evening journey, new morning); the last will. Pull-line is the book's creed. The staff emblem debuts the master device.
p1c23.palette_role: Full solar + serpent + white-gold noon highlight (color-mix solar+white 18%, text-verified noontide §50–51; finale privilege shared with no other P1 chapter). Staff gold densest metal in P1; serpent holy here (contrast p1c7's verbal knot — the same animal redeemed).
p1c23.opener: Staff emblem ≤160px (tallest art in P1) → part line → title → pull-line (the last will at the great noontide; the book's thesis in one sentence, quoted whole with its inner vow) → sun-rule 14rem. Neighbor contrast vs p1c22 (dusk tablet): dusk exhales, noon blazes — the part ends brighter than it began (dawn→noontide in 23 chapters; the solar-day arc kept). Class 'finale' (not 'emblem'): the slot treatment may carry extra air above/below per book CSS.
p1c23.reading: Finale measure 40rem (widest, with p1c1), gap 1.2em. Three movements (gift §1–25, earth §26–38, farewell §39–51) read on calm prose — no dividers per Rule 2; the pull-line + staff + white-gold cap carry the ceremony. Closes with the cresting-sun mini-seal (App. A.0) — Part I's last mark before Part II's Night-Ring.

p2c1.caption: I go new ways, a new speech has come to me…
p2c1.title: The Child with the Mirror
p2c1.rationale: Storm-dream converts to storm-joy; mirror-grin + lightning + lioness eyes.

p2c10.caption: Do not cease your dance, sweet girls!
p2c10.title: The Dance Song
p2c10.rationale: A dance that fails: round over sadness; Life's gold fishing-rod is the lure.

p2c11.caption: …only where there are graves are there resurrections.
p2c11.title: The Funeral Song
p2c11.rationale: Grief-voyage to the grave-island; the Will breaks graves — proleptic resurrection.

p2c12.caption: …I am that which must overcome itself again and again.
p2c12.title: Of Self-Overcoming
p2c12.rationale: Will-to-power: river, mirror, dice, egg in one vertical stack.

p2c13.caption: Still is the bottom of my sea: who could guess that it hides sportive monsters!
p2c13.title: Of the Sublime Men
p2c13.rationale: Pillar-virtue judges tiger-tension, ox-earth, thorns without a rose.

p2c14.caption: So now I love only my children’s land, the undiscovered land in the furthest sea…
p2c14.title: Of the Land of Culture
p2c14.rationale: Five motley masks + escaping sails: scorn of the masquerade, love of the future.

p2c15.caption: All sun-love is innocence and creative desire!
p2c15.title: Of Immaculate Perception
p2c15.rationale: Moon lechery converted to solar innocence across a dawn-blade diptych.

p2c16.caption: I have left the house of scholars and slammed the door behind me.
p2c16.title: Of Scholars
p2c16.rationale: Slam + flight: impact-rays, bitten wreath, poppy-ground; the cohort's smallest art.

p2c17.caption: …is the sea not the peacock of peacocks?
p2c17.title: Of Poets
p2c17.rationale: Sea/peacock vanity: wave-feather bravura + buffalo + dredged god-head; no earnest lyre.

p2c18.caption: The greatest events – they are not our noisiest but our stillest hours.
p2c18.title: Of Great Events
p2c18.rationale: Bellow vs stillness: cut-away volcano reveals the earth's gold heart — last gold.

p2c19.caption: Everything is empty, everything is one, everything is past!
p2c19.title: The Prophet
p2c19.rationale: The burst: grave-fortress torn open, thousand-peal motley laughter canopy.

p2c2.caption: The beauty of the Superman came to me as a shadow.
p2c2.title: On the Blissful Islands
p2c2.rationale: Harvest sermon; split fig + gold seeds + hammer; part's only early gold.

p2c20.caption: …until the creative will says to it: ‘But I willed it thus!’
p2c20.title: Of Redemption
p2c20.rationale: Bridge-dialogue: giant ear on a man-stalk over fragments; the redemption formula.

p2c21.caption: It is not the height, it is the abyss that is terrible!
p2c21.title: Of Manly Prudence
p2c21.rationale: Vertical abyss cleft: eye-up, hand-down, dragon's eye below; corona-less night.

p2c22.caption: It is the stillest words which bring the storm.
p2c22.title: The Stillest Hour
p2c22.rationale: Voiceless command; still clock, dove-trail, dew, dawn-break sliver.

p2c3.caption: Shame, shame, shame – that is the history of man!
p2c3.title: Of the Compassionate
p2c3.rationale: Pity made furniture: iron camp-bed, hard blanket, red disc half-hidden.

p2c4.caption: …pass them by quietly and with sleeping swords!
p2c4.title: Of the Priests
p2c4.rationale: Sleeping swords over a sleeping beast over a poison pool; one poppy promises rupture.

p2c5.caption: You want to be paid as well, you virtuous!
p2c5.title: Of the Virtuous
p2c5.rationale: Left-to-right argument: ploughshare tears, menagerie mocks, shells console.

p2c6.caption: Life is a fountain of delight; but where the rabble also drinks all wells are poisoned.
p2c6.title: Of the Rabble
p2c6.rationale: Disgust below, purity above, wind between; grins rhyme with the devil's.

p2c7.caption: …that is the bridge to my highest hope and a rainbow after protracted storms.
p2c7.title: Of the Tarantulas
p2c7.rationale: Web/pillar/rainbow: venom diagnosed, equality unmasked, self bound against revenge.

p2c8.caption: Like a sail, shuddering before the impetuosity of the spirit, my wisdom fares over the sea…
p2c8.title: Of the Famous Philosophers
p2c8.rationale: Sail above, desert below; the empty lion-skin is fame's costume with nobody in it.

p2c9.caption: Light am I: ah, that I were night!
p2c9.title: The Night Song
p2c9.rationale: Giver's solitude at totality; rising-only arcs; ring-form refrains crowned.

p3c1.caption: “In order to see much one must learn to look away from oneself – every mountain-climber needs this hardness.” — ¶12
p3c1.title: The Wanderer
p3c1.rationale: Midnight ridge-crossing soliloquy: the wanderer hardens himself for the last summit; cold summit vs yearning sea.
p3c1.palette_role: Noon blaze cools to midnight ridge: white-gold path-light on deepened night; bone figure, ember-free.
p3c1.opener: Full-bleed ridge scene above title; stacked (never overlaid) Cinzel title; mountain hardness voice.
p3c1.reading: Calm tablet prose; sea-yearning passages (¶18-26) carry their own rhythm, no styling.

p3c2.caption: “This long lane behind us: it goes on for an eternity. And that long lane ahead of us – that is another eternity.” — ¶21
p3c2.title: Of the Vision and the Riddle
p3c2.rationale: BOOK CENTERPIECE: the gateway Moment with two eternal lanes; dwarf of gravity; shepherd biting the serpent's head; transformed laughter. The recurrence doctrine staged as vision.
p3c2.palette_role: Full blaze frame: white-gold MOMENT legend, solar gateway, serpent-green coils, bone shepherd transfigured.
p3c2.opener: Gateway scene (portrait 400x500) above title; the two-lane pull-line; widest semantic opener in Part III.
p3c2.reading: Sermon-calm prose; courage anaphora (¶11-17) and shepherd transformation (¶40-41) unstylized — the vision carries them.

p3c3.caption: “When I have overcome myself in that, I will overcome myself in that which is greater; and a victory shall be the seal of my perfection!” — ¶25
p3c3.title: Of Involuntary Bliss
p3c3.rationale: Sea-voyage aftermath: afternoon bliss arrives unseasonably and is refused — Zarathustra stands ready for his deepest pain instead. Overcoming as the seal of perfection.
p3c3.palette_role: Afternoon gold held at bay: solar seal-voice against still luminous sea; refusal keeps the blaze framed, not flooding.
p3c3.opener: Open-door emblem (bliss refused entry) + seal-of-perfection pull-line; threshold-door grammar shared with p3c5/p3c7.
p3c3.reading: Calm prose; the refused-hour passage (¶30) reads as spoken dismissal, no styling.

p3c4.caption: “To stand over everything as its own sky, as its round roof, its azure bell and eternal certainty: and happy is he who thus blesses!” — ¶16
p3c4.title: Before Sunrise
p3c4.rationale: HYMN-SONG to the sky: mute friendship with the heavens, blessing as standing-over, chance dancing. Azure-bell crowns per identity spec.
p3c4.palette_role: Azure blaze: white-gold blessing on open-sky lapis; the brightest lyric ground in the book.
p3c4.opener: Azure-bell crown above centered lyric; sky-hymn voice; blessing pull-line.
p3c4.reading: CENTERED lyric: Spectral italic 1.15rem/2.0, 26-30rem; azure-bell stanza crowns; no drop cap (song).

p3c5.caption: “Everywhere I see lower doors: anyone like me can still pass through them, but – he has to stoop!” — ¶5
p3c5.title: Of the Virtue that Makes Small
p3c5.rationale: Satire of the small: houses like toy-boxes, low doors, sand-grain frankness, submission doctrines. The low-doors emblem literalizes the chapter's master image.
p3c5.palette_role: Diminished blaze: solar doors shrinking across the emblem; satire keeps gold architectural, never celebratory.
p3c5.opener: Low-doors emblem + stooping pull-line; satirical-tablet voice; doors grammar (p3c3/p3c5/p3c7).
p3c5.reading: Tablet prose with Cinzel solar drop cap; the grain-of-sand passage (¶30) unstylized.

p3c6.caption: “In the meanwhile, I run with warm feet hither and thither upon my mount of olives: in the sunny corner of my mount of olives do I sing and mock all pity.” — ¶35
p3c6.title: On the Mount of Olives
p3c6.rationale: Winter-song (closes 'Thus sang Zarathustra'): stern guest Winter, warm feet on the olive mount, silence that betrays nothing, mockery of pity. Olive-mount emblem per spec.
p3c6.palette_role: Snow-voice blaze: white-gold winter flame on olive-serpent; warmth inside cold, never ember.
p3c6.opener: Winter-flame crown above centered lyric; snow-voice; warm-feet pull-line closes the arc it opens.
p3c6.reading: CENTERED lyric: Spectral italic, winter-flame crowns; prose-cold frame stanzas centered with the song (whole-chapter song); no drop cap.

p3c7.caption: “By all that is luminous and strong and good in you, O Zarathustra! spit upon this city of shopkeepers and turn back!” — ¶15
p3c7.title: Of Passing By
p3c7.rationale: The great-city parable: ape-fool's warning, verbal swill, hanging-soul rags, newspapers from rags; Zarathustra passes by. City-gate emblem: the gate spat upon.
p3c7.palette_role: Noon glare on commerce: hard solar gate-lines, bone contempt; the city gets no softening tint.
p3c7.opener: City-gate emblem + spit-upon-the-gate pull-line; parable-contempt voice; third door/gate (p3c3/p3c5/p3c7).
p3c7.reading: Tablet prose, Cinzel solar drop cap; ape-dialogue exchanges read as spoken parable, no speaker styling.

p3c8.caption: “But it is a disgrace to pray! Not for everyone, but for you and me and for whoever else has his conscience in his head.” — ¶15
p3c8.title: Of the Apostates
p3c8.rationale: Lament over the pious-again apostates: meadow faded, dancers bent creeping to the cross, night-watchmen's dead gods. Disgrace-to-pray as the verdict.
p3c8.palette_role: Faded blaze: solar verdict against greyed meadow; elegiac gold, never festive.
p3c8.opener: Open-door emblem (the door the apostates crept back through) + disgrace pull-line; elegiac-sermon voice.
p3c8.reading: Tablet prose, Cinzel solar drop cap; night-watchman dialogue (¶28) unstylized.

p3c9.caption: “O Solitude! Solitude, my home! have lived too long wildly in wild strange lands to come home to you without tears!” — ¶0
p3c9.title: The Home-Coming
p3c9.rationale: Return-song: Solitude speaks as mother, crowd-noise confessed, poisonous flies of the good, soul sneezing sparkling wine. Vine-home warmth.
p3c9.palette_role: Home-fire blaze: white-gold vine arcade on hearth-warm lapis; tenderness the noon book rarely allows.
p3c9.opener: Vine-arcade crown above centered lyric; home-coming voice; tearful pull-line.
p3c9.reading: CENTERED lyric: Spectral italic, vine crowns; Solitude's long speech centered as song (whole-chapter song); no drop cap.

p3c10.caption: “In a dream, in my last morning dream, I stood today upon a headland – beyond the world, I held a pair of scales and weighed the world.” — ¶0
p3c10.title: Of the Three Evil Things
p3c10.rationale: Triptych-sermon: the scales dream weighs sensual pleasure, lust for power, selfishness — and blesses all three. Scales-triad emblem literalizes the weighing.
p3c10.palette_role: Dream-morning blaze: solar scales over rolling sea; triptych gold balanced, never flooding.
p3c10.opener: Scales-triad emblem + headland-dream pull-line; dream-weighing voice; triptych grammar echoes p1c2/p2c10 in noon hand.
p3c10.reading: Tablet prose, Cinzel solar drop cap; the three blessings (¶15+) read as calm decree.

p3c11.caption: “He calls earth and life heavy: and so will the Spirit of Gravity have it! But he who wants to become light and a bird must love himself – thus do I teach.” — ¶10
p3c11.title: Of the Spirit of Gravity
p3c11.rationale: The flying sermon: fool's hand, horse's foot, eagle's stomach; love of self against the Spirit of Gravity; the dwarf named and defied. Rope-ladder: the climb out of heaviness.
p3c11.palette_role: Ascent blaze: solar ladder-lines rising, serpent earth below; lightness rendered as line, not glow.
p3c11.opener: Rope-ladder emblem + love-yourself pull-line; flying-sermon voice; dwarf-gravity motif keys the gravity thread (p3c2/p3c11).
p3c11.reading: Tablet prose, Cinzel solar drop cap; body-catalogue (¶0-5) and oyster passage (¶20) unstylized.

p3c12.caption: “For creators are hard. And it must seem bliss to you to press your hand upon millennia as upon wax, bliss to write upon the will of millennia as upon metal – harder than metal, nobler than metal. Only the noblest is perfectly hard.” — ¶174
p3c12.title: Of Old and New Law-Tables
p3c12.rationale: THE GREAT SERMON (183 paras, longest chapter): shattered old tables, half-written new ones, laughing-lion sign awaited, Become-hard doctrine. Monumental tablets art; relief dividers ~every 30 paras.
p3c12.palette_role: Monumental blaze: full solar on shattered + half-written stone; the weightiest gold in Part III, earned by length.
p3c12.opener: Monumental tablets (seal-class) + Become-hard pull-line; law-giving voice; longest title in the book balanced ≤3 lines.
p3c12.reading: Tablet prose, Cinzel solar drop cap; relief dividers (p3-relief) above ¶30/60/90/120/150 breaks; no mid-text color.

p3c13.caption: “I, Zarathustra, the advocate of life, the advocate of suffering, the advocate of the circle – I call you, my most abysmal thought!” — ¶6
p3c13.title: The Convalescent
p3c13.rationale: Vision-dialogue: seven-day sickness, abysmal thought summoned, animals preach the eternal recurrence (hour-glass year), rosy apple, new lyre. Sickbed + recurrence-wheel scene.
p3c13.palette_role: Sickbed pallor inside blaze: bone convalescence, white-gold wheel turning above; abyss-voice greens held in the wheel.
p3c13.opener: Sickbed-wheel scene above title; advocate-of-the-circle pull-line; abyss-voice; stacked title.
p3c13.reading: Tablet prose, Cinzel solar drop cap (vision); animals' long speeches (¶49-54) read as spoken doctrine, no speaker styling.

p3c14.caption: “O my soul, I gave you new names and many-coloured toys, I called you ‘destiny’ and ‘encompassment of encompassments’ and ‘time’s umbilical cord’ and ‘azure bell’.” — ¶9
p3c14.title: Of the Great Longing
p3c14.rationale: Longing-song to the soul (25 'O my soul' anaphoras): rescue, washing, storm-rights, contempt, azure-bell naming; ends bidding the soul sing. Azure-bell crown shared with p3c4 (sky-song kinship).
p3c14.palette_role: Soul-blaze: azure-bell white-gold on twilight lapis; tenderest gold in Part III.
p3c14.opener: Azure-bell crown above centered lyric; soul-address voice; naming pull-line (the azure bell itself).
p3c14.reading: CENTERED lyric: Spectral italic, azure-bell crowns; anaphora carries its own rhythm; no drop cap.

p3c15.caption: “But all joy wants eternity, ‘– wants deep, deep, deep eternity!” — ¶31
p3c15.title: The Second Dance Song
p3c15.rationale: Dance-song with Life: golden bark on dark waters, castanets, crooked ways, Wisdom vs Life jealousy, midnight's voice answering with the roundelay's first form. Dance-measure crown; lyre-dance motif threads p2c10/p3c15.
p3c15.palette_role: Midnight-dance blaze: gold eternity-cry on night-dance lapis; lyre-lines in white-gold.
p3c15.opener: Dance-measure crown above centered lyric; dance-partner voice; eternity pull-line.
p3c15.reading: CENTERED lyric: Spectral italic, dance-measure crowns; Life's speeches centered with the song; no drop cap.

p3c16.caption: “Oh how should I not lust for eternity and for the wedding ring of rings – the Ring of Recurrence!” — ¶24
p3c16.title: The Seven Seals (or: The Song of Yes and Amen)
p3c16.rationale: SEAL-SONG finale: seven stanzas each closing 'For I love you, O Eternity!' — the Ring of Recurrence refrain sevenfold. Z5: seven DISTINCT round seals (seal-round-1..7 + arc), read sevenfold.
p3c16.palette_role: Sevenfold blaze: the Ring refrain in white-gold; seven seals each distinct; part-finale fullness.
p3c16.opener: Seven-seal arc above title + Ring-of-Recurrence pull-line; seal-song voice; the only opener with seven seals.
p3c16.reading: CENTERED lyric: Spectral italic, seven seal-round crowns (one per stanza, Z5); Eternity refrains bone-italic (gold graphic-only at verse size); no drop cap.

p4c1.caption: “Away, away my hook! In, down, bait for my happiness! Drop down your sweetest dew, honey of my heart!” — ¶20
p4c1.title: The Honey Offering
p4c1.rationale: White-haired fisher-Zarathustra casts honey as bait for human fishes; sunrise/noontide/sunset triple suns; triptych panel 1 (sun low-left).
p4c1.palette_role: Ember-led morning; solar gold reserved for the rod-line itself (graphic, not text).
p4c1.reading: Calm body; rod-casting ¶7 solar left rule; closing eye ¶21 as 1.15em benediction. No drop cap (emblem form).

p4c2.caption: “It is the Higher Man that cries for you!” — ¶4
p4c2.title: The Cry of Distress
p4c2.rationale: Prophet brings the cry; two shadows on the slab; Higher-Man dread under bright day; sound made visible once.
p4c2.palette_role: Ember ground first invaded by deepened-night sea bands.
p4c2.opener: Scene figure above title; stacked text (contrast discipline).
p4c2.reading: Cinzel solar drop cap (threshold voice); cry passages ¶3-5 Spectral italic + ember left rule.

p4c3.caption: “What do we kings matter!” — ¶11
p4c3.title: Conversation with the Kings
p4c3.rationale: Two shabby kings in yellowed pomp, laden ass, Sybil verse; first ass drawing (quoted haloed c17, wreathed c18).
p4c3.palette_role: Ember + faded pomp derivations (color-mix ember/lapis), no new hues.
p4c3.reading: Sybil verse ¶18-20 as LEFT-measure indented italic with thin sun-rule above; ass's Ye-a (¶17) Cinzel small display bone. No drop cap.

p4c4.caption: “But what I am master of and expert on is the leech’s brain – that is my world!” — ¶16
p4c4.title: The Leech
p4c4.rationale: Conscientious leech-man in the swamp: one hand's-breadth of ground, ten leeches on the arm, root-lines in dark water.
p4c4.opener: Emblem with heavier bottom ground-line, half-submerged feel.
p4c4.reading: ¶16 serpent left rule. No drop cap.

p4c5.caption: “Who still loves me? – offer me hot hands!” — ¶44
p4c5.title: The Sorcerer
p4c5.rationale: Sorcerer-actor's 52-paragraph lament collapsing into confession; storm-lit prostration; fallen mask at frame edge (¶55-56). SUPERVISOR RULING: left-measure lyric treatment (option a) — centered reserved for true songs.
p4c5.palette_role: Ember + night; lightning bone-white (no green-flash hue).
p4c5.reading: Prose frame calm; lament ¶1-52 LEFT-measure indented italic with hanging indent; refrain size-steps (Ha ha! / Away! Away! / Hangman-god ¶26 largest). No drop cap.

p4c6.caption: “For this old god no longer lives: he is quite dead.” — ¶39
p4c6.title: Retired from Service
p4c6.rationale: Last pope, unemployed holy: blessing hand, forest hut, two wolves, blind-eye keystone; courteous autumnal melancholy.
p4c6.palette_role: Bone line on ember-night; palest ember chapter.
p4c6.reading: God-history ¶22-24 soft bone left rule. No drop cap.

p4c7.caption: “Man, however, is something that must be overcome.” — ¶43
p4c7.title: The Ugliest Man
p4c7.rationale: Murderer of God in Serpent's Death valley; half-turned seated shape honoring 'do not look at me!'; slashed-eye keystone. DARKEST OPENER (near-black). SUPERVISOR: motif bestiary-ugliest APPROVED (rule 15).
p4c7.palette_role: Near-black deepened night, ember cliff bands; NO solar gold anywhere — only P4 opener without it.
p4c7.opener: Emblem; title +0.01em air (dread needs air, not a tracked label).
p4c7.reading: Riddle dialogue ¶3-6 indented +0.95em; murder confession ¶30-32 bordered inset, ember edge. No drop cap.

p4c8.caption: “If we do not alter and become as cows, we shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.” — ¶8
p4c8.title: The Voluntary Beggar
p4c8.rationale: Mountain sermonizer preaching rumination to cows; hillock from below, three calm cow heads, breath-wisp spirals. [title-inference] VERIFIED in full prose.
p4c8.palette_role: Serpent pasture-light + solar warmth inside ember frame; brightest ember emblem.
p4c8.reading: Rumination lesson ¶8-10 left-measure indented block with leader spacing; +10% paragraph air. No drop cap.

p4c9.caption: “Where is – my home? I ask and seek and have sought for it, I have not found it.” — ¶24
p4c9.title: The Shadow
p4c9.rationale: Free spirit's shadow: six foolish legs diminishing along the ridge, broken-backbone hitch, mirror/window-pane cold. Typographic lost-and-found.
p4c9.palette_role: Ember-night with star-silver derivation (color-mix bone/lapis, sanctioned).
p4c9.reading: Confession ¶9-24 ragged with increasing right indent toward 'Vanity!' (¶24); answer ¶25-31 snaps back to full measure. No drop cap.

p4c10.caption: “Soft! Soft! Has the world not just become perfect?” — ¶3
p4c10.title: At Noontide
